chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who bought from another man a house in a property belonging to him, with all its rights, while there was another house above it: does the upper house enter into the rights of the lower house, or not?
So he عليه السلام wrote: “He has no right except to what he purchased by its name and its location, if Allah wills.”

key_terms.اشْتَرَى: purchased; entered into a sale contract
key_terms.الْبَيْتُ الْأَعْلَى: the upper house; the structure above the sold house
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ الْأَسْفَلِ: the lower house; the specifically purchased lower unit
key_terms.بَيْتًا: a house; the property unit being sold
key_terms.بِاسْمِهِ: by its name; as explicitly designated in the sale
key_terms.بِجَمِيعِ حُقُوقِهِ: with all its rights; the attached rights associated with the sold property
key_terms.مَوْضِعِهِ: its location; the specified physical place of the purchased property

ai.seo_question: When buying a lower house with all its rights, is the upper house included in the sale?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the scope of property rights in a sale. It states that the buyer is entitled only to the specifically named and identified property, and that unspecified adjoining or upper structures are not automatically included.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3884 - Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, may Allah (swt) have mercy on him, wrote to Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan bin Ali (as)

regarding a man who purchased a house in a property with all its rights, and there was another house above it.
He asked whether the upper house is included in the rights of the lower house or not.
Imam (as) responded: "He is entitled only to what he purchased by its name and specified location, if Allah (swt) wills."
